B. PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING AGENDA ITEMS

C. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

D. PUBLIC HEARING
1. Staff report recommending that the Parking and Traffic Commission conduct a public hearing to:
a. Receive public comments regarding the termination of the Residential Permit Parking Program on

b. Provide direction to the City Engineer on how to proceed

   CITY OF INGLEWOOD

  One West Manchester Blvd., Inglewood, CA 90301
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A

  FEBRUARY 2024 MEETING MINUTES

A. OPENING CEREMONIES
1. Chairperson Hibler welcomed the commission and the public for their attendance and participation.
  Additionally, it was announced that Commissioner Richard Galindo will serve as Parking and Traffic
  Observer and will be the Chairperson’s second in case of absence.
2. Meeting was held at 7:05 pm (PST) in the Community Room A located in the first floor on 02/28/24
3. Attendees included Barbara Hibler, Richard Galindo, Kip Rudd, Brett C.S. Roberts, Lois Hale, Peter
  Puglese, Diana Maximo, William Thompson and Police Department Representative.

B. PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING AGENDA ITEMS
1. A Larch Street resident visited the Parking and Traffic Commission to share that the Residential Parking
  Permit Program is not favorable due to lack of computer access. Visitor parking is not as easy to obtain
  and is inconvenient. There are no parking controls to ensure the removal of non-resident parking.
2. Sixth Avenue residents spoke about ending the Residential Parking Permit Program on 6th Avenue from
  104th Street to 108th Street. The following comments were given on the matter.
 The resident did not receive any information to be included in the process prior to the implementation.
 Residents never had problems parking on the street before or after the stadium expansion.
 Residents see drivers speeding more than any other problem on the block.
 Residents are forced to pay due to the events in Sofi.
 No traffic impact has been observed after the implementation of the Sofia measure.

C. APPROVAL OF MINUTES
1. Approval of the Minutes for the Meeting held on January 24, 2024
 A motion to accept the meeting notes was made by Kip Rudd and seconded by Richard Galindo.
 The motion was carried by the following roll call vote: Barbara Hibler, Richard Galindo, Kip Rudd, Brett
  Roberts and Lois Hale. All commissioners approved the minutes of the meeting notes. There was no
  rejection or noes.

D. RESOLUTIONS
1. None

E. UNFINISHED BUSINESS
1. Diana Maximo and William Thomson provided an update on the following items. Commissioners will
  follow this issue and ask questions when necessary.
 Vehicles parked from West Boulevard to Crenshaw Blvd at Manchester Blvd are blocking the sidewalk.
 Ordinance Designating City-Owned Parking Facilities as Parking Meter Zones and Establishing Special
  Event Parking Rates & fine for Parking Meter Zones:
  https://www.cityofinglewood.org/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Item/16501?fileID=23365
2. Peter Puglese reported that the implementation of this plan will depend on the financial resources that
  the City can obtain. Finding funding will be the next steps to help with the Safe Routes to School Plan.
  Commissioners will follow this issue and ask questions when necessary.
 Active-Transportation-and-Safe-Routes-to-School-Plan-Adopted-May-17-2022:
  https://www.cityofinglewood.org/DocumentCenter/View/17698/Active-Transportation-and-Safe-Routes-to-School-Plan-Adopted-May-17-2022

F. NEW BUSINESS
1. There were no comments from Commissioners wishing to address any additional issues in the Parking
  and Traffic Commission.

G. PUBLIC HEARING
1. Public Comments on Termination of the Residential Parking Permit Program on 6th Avenue from 104th
  Street to 108th Street; and give instruction to the City Engineer on how to proceed.
 On the date of the meeting, Sixth Avenue residents were allowed to speak on the matter during public
  comments (regarding agenda items). Therefore, the Parking and Traffic Commissioners immediately
  directed the City Traffic Engineer to continue with the voting process.
 The motion to accept was made by Baraba Hibler and seconded by Lois Hale.
 The motion was carried by the following roll call vote: Barbara Hibler, Richard Galindo, Kip Rudd, Brett
  Roberts and Lois Hale. All five commissioners voted in favor of the application proceeding.
 There was no rejection or noes.

H. PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING OTHER MATTERS
1. Persons wishing to address the Parking and Traffic Commission on any matter connected with City
  business not elsewhere considered on the agenda may do so at this time.
 There were no comments wishing to address any additional issues

I. CHAIRPERSON AND COMMISSIONERS REMARKS
1. The members of the Parking and Traffic Commission will provide oral reports, including reports on City
  related travels where lodging expenses are incurred, and/or address any matters they deem of general
  interest to the public.
 Commissioners asked about future street closures and improvements in the city. Public Works can only
  provide information about the major construction project and announced that it will be something that
  will be made known to the commission immediately.
 The Commission was reminded that some of the street improvements were shared with the Commission
  in the October 2023 Agenda Package under Exhibit A (Commissioner Initiatives Information on Capital
  Improvement Project for Fiscal Year 2023/24). The list is attached to this meeting note for reference.

J. ANNOUNCEMENTS
1. It was announced that the next Traffic and Parking Commission meeting will be Wednesday, March 27,
  2024 at 7:00 p.m. m., 1st Floor, City Hall Community Room A, Inglewood City Hall One Manchester
  Boulevard, Inglewood, CA 90301

K. ADJOURNMENT
1. The Parking and Traffic Commission meeting ended at 8:25 PM PST.

TO:  Parking and Traffic Commission

FROM:  Peter Puglese PE, TE, City Traffic Engineer

SUBJECT:  Request to Amend Residential Permit Parking District for 117th Street from
  Dehn Avenue and Lemoli Avenue within District 11

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the Parking and Traffic Commission conduct a public hearing to:
1. Receive Public Comments regarding the termination of the Residential Permit Parking
  Program on 117th Street from Dehn Avenue and Lemoli Avenue within District 11; and
2. Provide direction to the City Engineer on how to proceed

BACKGROUND:
In June 2020, the City Council adopted a Citywide Residential Permit Parking Program. The
program is enforced 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, with two-hour parking Monday through
Sunday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. (Ordinance No. 20-09). The program was adopted to protect residential
communities more effectively and efficiently from non-resident vehicle intrusion.

On December 11, 2023, Public Works (PW) Department received a petition requesting the
removal of Residential Permit Parking on 117th Street from Dehn Avenue and Lemoli Avenue
within District 11. There is a count of twenty-four (24) properties that are within the limit. Sixteen
(16) valid signatures (one signature per residential unit) were submitted on the petition, resulting
in sixty-seven percent (67 %) of all households on the block signing the petition in favor of
removing the permit parking restrictions. On March 8, 2024, a notice was sent to all addresses
within the petition boundary to attend the March Traffic and Parking Commission meeting to
express their views on the matter.

DISCUSSION:
The Residential Permit Parking District Program encourages residents to use their driveways to
park their vehicles, when available, so that those without driveways can park on the street.
Therefore, Public Works staff requests the Parking and Traffic Commission to provide
instructions on how to proceed with the request by either approving the request to start the voting
process; or denying the request to end the processing of the petition.

  NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING
  Petition for Termination of Permit Parking in
  Residential Neighborhood
A petition has been submitted to the Inglewood Public Works Department requesting the termination of
residential permit parking within District 11 on 117th Street between Dehn Avenue and Lemoli Avenue.
Per Sections 3-75 to 3-79 of the Inglewood Municipal Code, this matter will be presented to the
Inglewood Parking and Traffic Commission at the time and place specified:

  Wednesday March 27, 2024 at 7:00 p.m.
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

This notice is being mailed to all addresses within the subject area. Any interested person may attend
this meeting and speak on this matter.

  Purpose of Public Hearing
The purpose of this public hearing is to give all residents of the subject area listed above an opportunity
to state their opinion of the subject matter. The purpose of the Residential Permit Parking Program is
to assure the availability to residents of some on-street (curbside) parking spaces within a neighborhood
where the patrons and/or employees of a nearby commercial or industrial facility are otherwise using
all available on-street parking spaces.

The Inglewood Parking and Traffic Commission will therefore be considering if the availability of on-
street parking is severely impacted and if the termination of a residential permit parking within District
11 on 117th Street between Dehn Avenue and Lemoli Avenue would be warranted. If it is determined
to be warranted, ballots will be mailed to each household within the subject area. If a Residential Permit
Parking District is terminated, all residents and visitors in this neighborhood will not be restricted from
parking on the public streets at any time; including during special events. If you have any questions
regarding this matter, or wish to express an opinion but are unable to attend the public hearing, please
contact the Inglewood Public Works Department at (310) 412-5333.

  En la Sala Comunitaria A en el Primer Piso
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

Este aviso se envía por correo a todas las direcciones dentro del área de asunto. Cualquier persona
interesada puede asistir a esta reunión y hablar sobre este tema.

  Propósito de la Audiencia Pública
El propósito de esta audiencia pública es dar a todos los residentes del área mencionada anteriormente
la oportunidad de expresar su opinión sobre el tema. El propósito del Programa de Permisos de
Estacionamiento Residencial es garantizar la disponibilidad para los residentes de algunos espacios
de estacionamiento en la calle (bordillo) dentro de un vecindario donde los clientes y/o empleados de
una instalación comercial o industrial cercana utilizan todos los espacios de estacionamiento
disponibles en la calle. La Comisión de Tráfico y Estacionamiento de Inglewood, por lo tanto,
considerará si la disponibilidad de estacionamiento en la calle se ve gravemente afectada y si se
justificaría la terminación de un permiso de estacionamiento residencial dentro del Distrito 11 en 117th
Street entre Dehn Avenue y Lemoli Avenue. Si se determina que está justificado, las boletas se
enviarán por correo a cada hogar dentro del área en cuestión.

Si se rescinde un Distrito de Estacionamiento con Permiso Residencial, no todos los residentes y
visitantes de este vecindario tendrán restricciones para estacionar en las calles públicas en cualquier
momento; incluso durante eventos especiales. Si tiene alguna pregunta sobre este asunto o desea
expresar una opinión pero no puede asistir a la audiencia pública, comuníquese con el Departamento
de Obras Públicas de Inglewood al (310) 412-5333.
